booster.propellant_mass.ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship (Block 3; Wikipedia Super Heavy page says 3400 t for earlier blocks)

booster.engine_ring_outer.radius.ref: nozzle centres on ring about 0.5 m inside the 4.5 m skirt; 20 x 1.3 m nozzles need at least 4.0 m at 1.26 m spacing

booster.engine_ring_mid.radius.ref: 10 gimballing engines; 15 m circumference gives 1.5 m spacing

booster.engine_ring_centre.radius.ref: 3 engines mutually 108-108-144 deg per NSF/search summary https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/05/super-heavy-block-3-booster-future/

booster.engine_ring_mid.clock_offset.ref: mid ring rotated for pad deflector; amount unknown; 18 deg would be half pitch of 36 deg, 9 deg chosen as placeholder

raptor3.nozzle_exit_diameter_sl.ref: Raptor 2 ~1.3 m; Raptor 3 similar or slightly smaller; not verified in this run

raptor3.length_sl.ref: Raptor 2 sea-level ~3.1 m; Raptor 3 slightly shorter

raptor3.rvac_nozzle_exit_diameter.ref: RVac about 2.4 m per general knowledge; not confirmed by search

booster.engine_plane_y.ref: reference origin: nozzle exit plane; thrust plate about 3.2 m above

booster.engine_thrust_plate_height.ref: aft skirt with four 1.4 m rings starts about 3-5 m up; V3 engines mounted on steel plate not dome (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/05/super-heavy-block-3-booster-future/)

booster.common_dome_height.ref: fits photo frost boundary at y=366 px => 45 m up; propellant split about 78/22 by mass (O/F 3.6) gives about 57/43 by volume

booster.hot_stage_zone.bottom_height.ref: integrated open N1-style truss hot-stage, exhaust hits booster forward dome (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/05/super-heavy-block-3-booster-future/)

booster.hot_stage_zone.height.ref: 72.3 minus 62; vented open truss with about 12 struts

booster.hot_stage_vent_count.ref: placeholder for the vent bays in the open truss; unverified

booster.grid_fin.azimuth_deg.ref: 3 fins equally spaced (V3), relative to catch-pin axis; orientation of fin 1 not verified

booster.grid_fin.hinge_height.ref: lower than V2 (V2 fins about 69 m), placed at base of hot-stage truss

booster.grid_fin.span.ref: V2 fin about 2.9 x 3.3 m scaled to give 1.5x area (ratio 1.22 each side)

booster.catch_pin_count.ref: two pins on opposite sides for chopsticks

booster.catch_pin_height.ref: in hot-stage region above CH4 tank; Pad 2 chopsticks are about 10 m shorter than Pad 1 (https://nasaspaceflight.com/2025/08/starbase-pad-2-advancements-pad-1/)

booster.raceway_count.ref: cable raceways run along the booster length

ship.length.ref: 124 m stack (src SFN) minus 72.3 m booster = 51.7; V2 ship 52.1 m (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship_(spacecraft)). Wikipedia lists Block 3 ship as 61 m (est) which contradicts the 124 m stack; rejected

ship.rvac.radius.ref: centre triangle of 3 RVac with 2.4 m nozzles; spacing 2.9 m

ship.rsl.radius.ref: 3 sea-level engines in outer ring, clocked 60 deg from RVacs

ship.aft_flap.hinge_height.ref: side of engine bay/LOX tank; V2 aft flap about 9 x 4 m

ship.aft_flap.size.ref: length x chord; photo flare 26 px wide about 15.5 m

ship.forward_flap.hinge_height.ref: just below nose cone base; V2/V3 thinner, angled about 140 deg (src W3 for angle)

ship.nose.height.ref: tangent ogive; tip radius about 0.3 m; header tanks in nose

ship.nose.tip_radius.ref: photo tip 5 px wide about 3 m at blur; real tip smaller

ship.common_dome_height.ref: LOX below, CH4 above; O/F 3.6 gives about 58% of tank volume LOX

ship.header_tank_height.ref: LOX and CH4 header tanks in the nose; V2 had them inside the nose cone/payload bay

ship.tile.coverage.ref: photo: ship looks black over full visible length

ship.leeward.colour.ref: not visible in photo; 304L tumbled finish

ship.qd_plate.height.ref: ship quick-disconnect / QD plate near forward end of the tank section; Block 3 adds refuelling hardware (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship)

stack.hot_stage_gap.ref: ship engine bells nested in booster hot-stage truss at liftoff

scene.tower_height.ref: photo geometry gives about 125-140; Pad 2 tower cited around 146 m in general sources

scene.tower_offset_xz.ref: tower left of rocket and behind it in the image; sign depends on camera look direction (about north). Very uncertain

scene.camera_estimate.ref: photo scale: 0.6 m/px, assumed 74 deg hfov

scene.liftoff_height_of_booster_base.ref: photo: base at tower-top height, about 145 m
